ground_truth_issues.description: A test creates three distinct recovery artifacts for the same account through the real recovery flow and proves only the third/newest artifact can complete recovery.
A test proves both earlier artifacts from a three-artifact sequence are rejected and cannot change the password.
A test attempts recovery with a stale artifact, then proves the current newest artifact is still usable afterward.
A test completes recovery with the newest artifact, then proves that exact newest artifact cannot be reused.
A test completes recovery with the newest artifact, then proves all older superseded artifacts remain unusable afterward.
A test uses two independent clients where client A obtains an artifact, client B obtains a newer artifact for the same account, and client A's older artifact is rejected.
A test uses independent clients in overlapping recovery flows and proves the final account password can only be set by the newest valid artifact.
A test issues concurrent or near-concurrent recovery requests and proves exactly one resulting artifact can complete recovery.
A test proves passwords attempted through losing or stale concurrent artifacts cannot be used to authenticate.
A test proves a failed stale-artifact recovery attempt does not change password state, invalidate the newest artifact, or corrupt later login behavior.
A test verifies the authentication matrix after recovery: old password fails, stale-artifact password fails, and newest-artifact password succeeds.
Tests use independent persistent clients or cookie jars for multi-request and cross-client recovery behavior.
